title: "import/no-named-as-default-member"
description: "Disallow reading a property of a default import that is also a named export of the module"
# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.
plugin: "import"

After `import config from "./config"`, `config.load` is a property of the default export. It isn't the module's named export `load`. If the default export doesn't have that property, you get `undefined`. If it does, a named import says the same thing more directly and lets bundlers drop the exports you don't use.

The rule reads the imported module and reports `config.load` and `const { load } = config` if the module has a named export `load`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"import/no-named-as-default-member" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* file "config.js" */}
```js config.js
export function load(path) {
  return JSON.parse(read(path));
}

export default { port: 3000 };
```

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
import config from "./config";

config.load("./app.json");
const { load } = config;
```

Not reported:

{/* file "config.js" */}
```js config.js
export function load(path) {
  return JSON.parse(read(path));
}

export default { port: 3000 };
```

{/* good */}
```js
import config, { load } from "./config";

load("./app.json");
listen(config.port);
```
